title: Perception, Quality, and Accuracy of Sunscreen Content on TikTok: SkinMedia Cross-Sectional Content Analysis
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of the 100 most-liked English-language TikTok videos returned by the search term 'sunscreen'. Each video's accuracy was coded as accurate / inaccurate / mixed / opinion-based by concordance with American Academy of Dermatology sunscreen guidelines, and the paper reports 6 (6%) of the 100 videos as inaccurate. Guideline concordance stated as accurate/inaccurate is an external ground truth, so this is a CONTENT share with a stated denominator and the paper is eligible. The Global Quality Score results are recorded separately as QUALITY.

estimates.country: not stated (English-language TikTok videos; US-based investigators, American Academy of Dermatology guidelines as the benchmark)
estimates.measure_type: % of the 100 most-liked TikTok 'sunscreen' videos coded inaccurate against American Academy of Dermatology sunscreen guidelines
estimates.value_raw: 6 (6%) of 100 videos inaccurate; in the same breakdown 35 (35%) accurate, 2 (2%) mixed, 57 (57%) opinion-based or not applicable
estimates.denominator: 100 most-liked English-language TikTok videos returned by the search term 'sunscreen' under TikTok's 'most-liked' filter on 14 August 2024, from newly created accounts to reduce algorithmic personalisation (top 106 retrieved; ranks 101-106 reserved for calibration)
estimates.definition: A video was coded 'inaccurate' when its factual content was discordant with the American Academy of Dermatology sunscreen guidelines; videos with no checkable factual claims were coded 'opinion-based', and videos with both accurate and inaccurate elements were coded 'mixed' and are NOT in this numerator
estimates.misinfo_def: "Accuracy was categorized as accurate, inaccurate, mixed, or opinion-based, according to concordance with the American Academy of Dermatology sunscreen guidelines"
estimates.source_quote: Out of the 100 videos, 35 (35%) were classified as accurate, 6 (6%) as inaccurate, 2 (2%) as mixed, and 57 (57%) were opinion-based or not applicable for factual accuracy evaluation.
estimates.page_loc: Results, Descriptive Overview; Table 1 (Accuracy); repeated in Abstract and Discussion, Principal Findings
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two reviewers (KD, JR-M) developed a structured codebook on 6 calibration videos, trained to interrater reliability >0.90 across variables, then one reviewer coded all 100 videos with the second independently coding a blinded 10% subset: agreement 97.9%, Scott pi 0.954, Cohen kappa 0.954, Krippendorff alpha 0.956. Ground truth was the American Academy of Dermatology sunscreen guidance. GQS agreement was weaker (kappa 0.712).
estimates.moderator_quote: The final search was conducted on August 14, 2024, using newly created TikTok accounts to reduce algorithmic personalization. We applied TikTok's "most-liked" filter and identified the top 106 most-liked videos returned by the search term "sunscreen."
estimates.notes: This is a strict numerator: it counts only videos coded inaccurate, and excludes the 2 (2%) 'mixed' videos. Adding them would give 8/100, but that is a cross-category sum I would have computed and is barred by R8, so it is not extracted; the component counts are in value_raw so an adjudicator can decide. The 57% 'opinion-based or not applicable' category means only 43 of the 100 videos were actually appraisable for factual accuracy - an alternative denominator (6/43 = 14%) is nowhere stated in the paper and is therefore not extracted. Rank-truncated most-liked set on a single topic, hence denom_scope=topical with denom_selection=curated. Country is not stated; the search was English-language only and benchmarked to US (AAD) guidance, so a defensible alternative coding is United States - flagged for the adjudicator.

estimates.country: not stated (English-language TikTok videos; US-based investigators)
estimates.measure_type: % of the 100 most-liked TikTok 'sunscreen' videos rated poor or below-average quality (Global Quality Score of 1 or 2)
estimates.denominator: 100 most-liked English-language TikTok videos returned by the search term 'sunscreen' on 14 August 2024
estimates.definition: A video scored 1 (poor: largely missing information or unhelpful for viewer use) or 2 (below average: minimal content with major omissions) on the 5-point Global Quality Score, with anchors revised by the authors to reflect viewer-facing usefulness and clarity
estimates.misinfo_def: "Accuracy was categorized as accurate, inaccurate, mixed, or opinion-based, according to concordance with the American Academy of Dermatology sunscreen guidelines"
estimates.source_quote: The majority (71/100, 71%) of videos received GQS of 1 (poor quality) or 2 (below average), with only 2 (2%) scoring a 5 (excellent quality).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Global Quality Score (Bernard et al 5-point scale) with author-revised anchors emphasising lay-viewer usefulness; coded by the same two trained reviewers, GQS-specific Cohen kappa 0.712 (the weakest variable, which the authors attribute to the scale's known subjectivity).
estimates.moderator_quote: Content quality or usability was assessed using the 5-point GQS described by Bernard et al [ 10 ] (1=poor to 5=excellent); in our study, GQS anchors emphasized viewer-facing usefulness and clarity
estimates.notes: QUALITY, not CONTENT: GQS measures completeness and usefulness for viewers, so a wholly accurate video can score 1 for being thin or unclear. Excluded from prevalence. The 71/100 figure is stated verbatim in the Results, so it is not a sum I computed from the GQS distribution.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, with reasons: (a) 2 (2%) 'mixed' accuracy videos - kept out of the CONTENT numerator because combining them with the 6 inaccurate videos would be a cross-category sum barred by R8; recorded in value_raw instead. (b) 35 (35%) accurate and 57 (57%) opinion-based - the accurate share is the converse of the construct, and 'opinion-based' is an unappraisability category, not misinformation. (c) Promotional content in 27 (27%) videos - commercial disclosure, not falsity. (d) 'Used references 0 (0%)' - sourcing practice, not falsity. (e) Creator-credential shares (18/100 health care professionals, 13 dermatologists) and thematic content shares (toxicity 10%, specific ingredients 13%, SPF 30%, sun safety education 31%, non-white-skin content 14%) - topic/creator descriptors. (f) Engagement means for inaccurate vs accurate videos (2,141,683 vs 2,732,594 mean views) and all correlation coefficients including the decile analysis (accuracy vs views r = -0.720) - these are associations and per-video means, not shares of exposure, so no EXPOSURE or REACH row; note the paper reports no total-view-weighted share of inaccurate content, which would have been the exposure-side estimate. (g) Figures cited from other papers - Haff et al mean DISCERN 1.58/5, Khan et al mean DISCERN 2.68/5, Kearney et al '69% of videos under sunscreen conspiracy searches were antisunscreen', Hales et al '26% of daytime skincare regimens included sunscreen' - excluded per R8 as values the paper cites from elsewhere. FOR THE ADJUDICATOR: Table 1's attitude rows (Positive 74, Negative 7, Neutral 9) sum to 90 and contradict the Results text ('74 (74%) videos, with the remainder split between 17 (17%) neutral and 9 (9%) negative'); this internal inconsistency does not touch the accuracy or GQS rows I extracted, but it is a mark against the paper's reporting care.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis; single neutral search term 'sunscreen' on TikTok, 14 August 2024, from newly created accounts to reduce personalisation, 'most-liked' filter, top 106 retrieved and top 100 analysed (English or English-subtitled, sunscreen-relevant; duplicates and irrelevant excluded; ranks 101-106 used only for calibration). Structured codebook; two reviewers calibrated to IRR >0.90 with iterative anchor revision, then one reviewer coded all 100 videos and a second independently coded a blinded 10% subset (agreement 97.9%, Scott pi 0.954, Cohen kappa 0.954, Krippendorff alpha 0.956; GQS kappa 0.712). No missing data. IRB-exempt (no human participants). Limitations acknowledged: most-liked-only selection, cross-sectional snapshot, GQS subjectivity.
